behavior_contracts.C9.2: checks::require(bool condition, str reason) -> void emits [checks::failed]; checks::failed(str reason) is ordinary nominal domain data at core ID 1010. Condition then reason evaluate once each under ordinary call semantics; the reason evaluates even when true and argument-evaluation failures stay at the caller boundary. True completes void; false produces a fresh occurrence with the exact authored reason, call-site span and invocation path in private diagnostic metadata. The bound is always [checks::failed] including literal-true calls; callers match or forward via relay call/explicit arms. [_] does not catch it. Attached assertions use existing complete-error constructor expectations; harness violations stay independently sticky; timeout/crash never counts as an expected check. No new keyword, standard category, or assertion DSL.

scope_note: Only the named require-helper idiom was migrated. Inline unreachable-branch markers of the form false/_ => do int invalid = 1 / 0 (generics, coordination, native, bytes, codec, callables, assertions, cli, arrays fixtures) and arithmetic-trap tests (parser/offline, project inert-init, 1.0/0.0 sort) are untouched: the former guard control-flow reachability rather than reporting a named check with a reason, and AE29's evidence clauses (helper+callers migration, C9.2 library, recovery, negatives, runtime/fixture/lowering) are all satisfied without changing their bounds. Timeout/crash non-pass behavior is inherited from the LF04 supervised suites, referenced not duplicated.
